Le lundi 1 février 2016 22:57:47 UTC+8, Alexander Bertram a écrit :
> Hi Joël,
> It looks like e1071 has C++ code which our toolchain does not yet compile. (Issue #119 <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/119>)
>
> The message you're seeing is only a warning because the Java class that will eventually contain the compiled C/C++ code is missing.
>
> If there are functions in e1071 that don't rely on the C/C++ code, then they should work fine, but unfortunately any functions which rely on C/C++ for this package will fail.
>
> We're making good progress on the native code compiler, but unfortunatley for this package at least, we're not there yet.
>
> Alex
>
>

messages.subject: Re: SVM (e1071) from Java
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,
It looks like this was caused by a regression in our C++ compiler related to void type inference [1]. I've just commited a fix [2] and a new build of both Renjin and e1071 package is now available [3].

Best,
Alex

[1] http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/e1071/1.6-8/test/svm-examples/history
[2] https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/7f1e5306a741e2800204d06ffbfc23d83db46536
[3] http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/e1071/1.6-8

messages.subject: Re: srand was found at compile-time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Changxin,

It looks like the C code in the e1071 package makes a call to the C standard library function "srand" [1], which was not implemented in Renjin's C library [2].

Normally, packages are supposed to generate random numbers through R's API, but I guess some packages can include a stray reference here and there to the C standard library's routines, so I've added wrappers around Java's Random class [3]. Perhaps we should automatically transform calls to srand() and rand() to calls into the R session's random number generator? I'm not sure how this will affect the behavior so I've left it simple for now.

A new build of e1071 1.5-22 is now available with this fix [4].

You might also consider using the latest version of e1071, as it is (again) compatible with Renjin after another fix today.

Best,
Alex

[1] http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/cstdlib/srand/
[2] https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/tools/gcc-bridge/runtime/src/main/java/org/renjin/gcc/runtime/Stdlib.java
[3] https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/e43999813392f694dc3f983a18ffd177cf1ba089
[4] http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/e1071/1.5-22

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Alain for this huge contribution, and congratulations on your new contract!

I will take some time to merge in the final pull request.

The failing test is probably due to the way Renjin handles file paths: all file i/o is done on a virtual file system so paths might look like file:///home/alex/readme.txt or jar://....

So rather than calling java i/o directly, you should go through Native.currentContext().resolveFile(()

Thanks again,

Alex
